title: Pay your NSW ambulance fee
summary: This page provides instructions on how to pay an NSW ambulance fee online if you have received a bill.
intro:
If you've received a bill for your NSW ambulance service, you can pay online.

Ambulance fees are based on a call out charge plus a per kilometre charge, based on the round trip between the ambulance station, pick up address, destination and return to the ambulance station.

Medicare doesn't cover the costs.

Ambulance fee exemptions: some ambulance services are provided free of charge to people who meet certain criteria.
who_can_apply: Anyone who has received an invoice can pay the NSW ambulance fee.
Exemptions may apply if you are a pensioner and concession card holder, a resident with private health insurance, or eligible for other exemptions.
what_you_need: Your payment reference number (found in the 'How to pay' section of the invoice).
The issue date (found in the box on the top right hand corner of the invoice).

how_to_steps.text: Enter your payment reference number and the issue date.
Check the 'I'm not a robot' box.

more_info.text: The NSW government subsidises 49% of ambulance fees for NSW residents only.
If you're finding it difficult to pay the fee, you can arrange for a payment plan or apply for a fee review.
If you're exempt from payment, provide your details online.
If you don't pay your ambulance bill, it will be given to Revenue NSW to deal with.

faqs.q: How are NSW ambulance fees calculated?
faqs.a: Ambulance fees are based on a call out charge plus a per kilometre charge, calculated on the round trip between the ambulance station, pick up address, destination, and return to the ambulance station.

faqs.q: Does Medicare cover the NSW ambulance fee?
faqs.a: No, Medicare does not cover the costs of the ambulance fee.

faqs.q: Who can pay the NSW ambulance fee online?
faqs.a: Anyone who has received an invoice can pay the NSW ambulance fee.
